$comment: The free half of Code Connect.
Figma's Code Connect stores this mapping inside the Figma file and needs a
Dev or Full seat on an Organization or Enterprise plan. IonBase is not for
people who can afford that and nobody else, so the mapping lives here: in
git, reviewable, free, and checked against BOTH sides on every build.
Left side  figma/components.json  — what the Figma component actually is
Right side dist/meta/components.json — what the React component actually is
scripts/verify-figma-map.mjs fails the build if either side moves. That is
the part Code Connect does not give you: it will happily publish a mapping
onto a prop that was renamed last week.
Output: dist/figma-map.json, keyed by Figma node id AND by Figma component
name, so an agent holding either can resolve the real component.
BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE CHECKED. "unmapped" answers "this Figma component has
no React counterpart, and here is why". "codeUnmapped" answers the reverse:
this React component has nothing in Figma. Without it, a component that is
drawn later would be silently missing from Dev Mode forever — the same
silence the Figma-side gate exists to break.

Show Separator#1359:4.ignore: The separator is a CSS ::before in code and never markup, so it stays out of the accessibility tree — a "/" in the DOM is the usual build of this component and the usual defect. Figma has no generated content, so it is drawn as a real text layer and switched off on the first crumb. A drawing convenience with no prop behind it.

Change.note: Figma draws what the badge SAYS; code derives it from two props. The direction is the sign of `change` (Up is positive), and Better or Worse follows from that and goodWhen — so Worse Up is a rise where down was good. No Change is a `change` that rounds to zero; None is `change` omitted. The badge text itself is computed from `change` and `changeUnit`.

Empty.ignore: the drawn form of an empty value. In code pass null (not a typed dash): the item draws the "—" and reads the list's emptyText, "Not set"

unmapped..Status Indicator:
The dot Avatar draws in its corners. Avatar owns both instances — Top is Intent=Primary with the check glyph, Bottom is Intent=Success with Show Icon off — and exposes them as `topIndicator` / `bottomIndicator`.

The leading dot in the name is Figma's own marker for a private component: it is excluded from the published library, so a designer cannot place one on a canvas even if they wanted to. That settles a question this entry used to argue: it is internal by the file's own declaration, not merely by our reading of it. The same call Line, Progress and Progress Heading get for being internal to ScrollProgress — with better evidence.

Map it only if the dot is ever removed.
unmapped.Calendar: The open calendar both pickers render internally — Calendar and CalendarPopover are not exported, because a grid with no field to own its value is not a control a caller should mount. Mode=Single is DatePicker’s, Mode=Range is DateRangePicker’s; Months=Two is `visibleMonths={2}`, Show Presets is `presets` and Show Clear is `isClearable`, all on DateRangePicker. Drawn separately because a frame cannot both hug a field and overlay a grid on it — the same reason Combobox Menu is its own frame.
unmapped.Calendar Day: A day cell inside Calendar — internal to it the way Pagination Item is internal to Pagination. A caller never places one; `isDateUnavailable`, `minValue` and `maxValue` on the pickers decide which state each day draws in.
unmapped.Chart Legend Item: One entry of Chart Legend — `items[n]` in code, `{ label, series }`. Its Shape follows the legend’s `shape`; Series picks chart/1…8. Internal to the legend.
unmapped.Chart Tooltip Row: One entry of Chart Tooltip — `rows[n]` in code, `{ label, value, series }`. Series picks the swatch from chart/1…8, exactly as `series` does. Internal to the tooltip the way Pagination Item is internal to Pagination.
unmapped.Combobox Menu: The list Combobox opens. It is not a separate export: the React component renders its own menu, because the two are one control and splitting them would let a caller mount a listbox with no combobox to own it. Drawn separately in Figma because a frame cannot both hug a field and overlay a list on top of it.
unmapped.Command Palette Item: One row of the palette, drawn so Active and Disabled can be seen. There is no code export behind it and there should not be: rows are built from the palette's `commands` array, where the Label, Description, Icon and shortcut are fields of one command — `label`, `description`, `icon`, `shortcut` — and Active is the keyboard's position, not a prop. The same call Combobox Menu gets.
unmapped.Form Field: Label, helper text and error wiring are built into Input and Select rather than a separate wrapper — the wrapper is how Figma composes them, not how React does.
unmapped.Line: An internal part of the Scroll Progress rail, not a component a caller composes.
unmapped.Pagination Item: The cell inside Pagination — a page number, an arrow or the truncation ellipsis. Figma needs it as its own set to hold the Size x State matrix; a caller never places one, so it is internal to Pagination the way Line and Progress are internal to Scroll Progress.
unmapped.Screen Frame: The frame FullCard draws around its media slot. The component owns it, so there is nothing for a caller to place.
unmapped.Side Menu Item: A 32-tall side-navigation row on the Side Menu page, which predates Sidebar. It shared the name Menu Item with the real one (82:217) until 25 Sep 2026, and because the export keyed on the name it silently replaced it — the mapping, the gates and the Dev Mode block all pointed here. Sidebar Item is the side-navigation row code ships.
unmapped.Side Menu Section Title: The section heading of the same pre-Sidebar side menu. Menu Section Title (1468:271) is the menu's own, drawn on the Menu page; Sidebar Section is the side navigation's.
unmapped.Table/Cell Text: TableCell covers Figma's Table Cell and Cell Text together; the two are never used apart in the design. Recorded in TableCell's contract.
unmapped.Multi Select Menu: The list MultiSelect opens, with a check on each row. Not a separate export, for Combobox Menu's reason: the list and the field are one control, and a listbox with nothing to own it is not a thing a caller should be able to mount. Drawn separately because a frame cannot both hug a field and overlay a list.
unmapped.Tree View Item: One row of Tree View — `items[n]` in code, `{ id, label, icon, description, children, isDisabled }`. There is no row export and there should not be: the tree builds its rows from `items`, because a row's level, position among its siblings and open state are the tree's to know, not the row's. Kind is whether the item has `children` and is in `expandedKeys`; Level is its depth; State Selected is `selectedKeys`, Disabled is `isDisabled`, Hover and Focus are runtime. Label, Icon and Description are the item's fields; Show Check follows the tree's `selectionMode="multiple"`.
unmapped.List Item: One row of List — `items[n]` in code, `{ id, label, description, leading, meta, href, isDisabled }`, plus the list's `renderActions(item)`. There is no row export: the list builds its rows from `items`, because a row's keyboard position, selection and link behaviour are the list's to know. Selection follows the list's `selectionMode` (Multiple draws the Checkbox); State Selected is `selectedKeys`, Disabled is `isDisabled`, Hover and Focus are runtime. Label and Description are the item's fields; Show Leading, Show Meta and Show Actions are whether `leading`, `meta` and `renderActions` are given.

codeUnmapped.DateRangePicker: Drawn, but not as a set of its own: its field is Date Picker Type=Range and its calendar is Calendar Mode=Range. A Figma set maps to exactly one code component, and splitting one field into two sets to satisfy that would draw the same box twice. Read Date Picker’s Type note for the handoff.
codeUnmapped.Icon: Figma has no Icon component; icons are vector assets dropped into slots. Icon is the React wrapper that gives any of them a size rung and an accessible label, so there is nothing on the Figma side to point at.
codeUnmapped.LogoMark: Logo-Ionbase maps to Logo. Figma spells the no-wordmark case as that component's Type axis rather than a separate component; LogoMark is how code spells the same thing.
codeUnmapped.RadioGroup: Figma draws Radio only. The group is the thing that owns the selected value, which a static frame cannot express — Figma's Radio State axis is ignored for exactly this reason. Its label, help, error and orientation are the shell drawn as Checkbox Group; the two groups share it in code as well.
codeUnmapped.ScrollProgress: Drawn in Figma as its three parts — Line, Progress, Progress Heading — all of which the component owns internally. There is no whole-component frame to map.
codeUnmapped.Table: Figma draws Table Row and Table Cell; the table itself is the caller assembling them. Density, the one property Table owns, is mapped on Table Cell.
codeUnmapped.TableHead: As Table — a code-side grouping element. Figma expresses a header row as a Table Row variant, not a separate component.
codeUnmapped.ToastProvider: Figma draws Toast, which is mapped. The provider is placement, queueing and the live region — runtime behaviour with nothing to draw.
codeUnmapped.MenuTrigger: Composition, not a drawing: a Button followed by a Menu, both already drawn and mapped. What MenuTrigger adds — open state, positioning, aria-haspopup and aria-expanded, focus on open and return on close — is runtime behaviour a static frame cannot hold, the same reason RadioGroup is here.
codeUnmapped.Fieldset: Drawn as the shell of Checkbox Group: the legend, the helper and the Error recolour are Form Field's type, laid around a set of options. A Fieldset of Inputs is the caller composing Form Fields under that legend, so there is no separate frame to point at.
codeUnmapped.SidePanelLayout: Layout, not a drawn component: the flex row a SidePanel sits in, content first. In Figma the Side Panel is placed beside the content on the frame; there is no row to draw.
codeUnmapped.ContextMenu: Draws nothing of its own: what opens is Menu — the same Menu component, rows and sections as the thing's ⋯ menu — placed at the pointer instead of under a button. A second Menu set drawn for it would be a copy that drifts. Design the menu as Menu; where it opens is behaviour.
